subject: Order Form: pricing anchor, true-up cadence & EU withholding treatment
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@acme.io>, procurement@acme.io
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-31T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order Form: pricing anchor, true-up cadence & EU withholding treatment

Hi Elena / Acme procurement team —

Attaching our latest Order Form (OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) and a small EU tax matrix (EU_tax_matrix.xlsx) that maps the withholding scenarios we discussed. Before we send this to Legal for a formal redline, quick asks so we can land commercial terms consistently with Finance: 

1) Pricing anchor: We proposed a Year 1 anchor based on a blended usage band (Tiered usage + seat cap) on page 2. Please confirm which metric Acme wants to anchor on (monthly active devices vs total API calls). That determines the min-commit calculation.

2) Minimum commit true-up cadence: We recommend quarterly true-ups with billing in advance + a quarterly true-up invoice/credit. Confirm acceptance of quarterly cadence or whether you need monthly true-ups instead.

3) Net terms & PO: Our standard is Net 60 for enterprise orders of this size. You referenced Net 45 in the call — is that a hard requirement? If Acme requires Net 45, we can do a one-time concession but need Finance approval. Also please confirm the billing entity (US corp vs EU subsidiary) and provide the PO template (if you have one) so we can ensure the PO matches the Order Form.

4) EU withholding/tax treatment: The EU tax matrix notes common withholding rates by country. If Acme’s EU entity will withhold tax, we need the tax certificate within 60 days of payment to issue a back-credit. If you expect routine withholding, we need to add a gross-up or VAT evidence clause — see suggested language below.

Suggested interim language (for Legal to refine):
- "If Customer withholds any taxes from payments due under this Order Form, Customer shall provide Redwood with official tax withholding documentation within sixty (60) days of payment. Upon receipt, Redwood will issue a credit or refund for the withheld amount. If withholding would reduce Redwood’s net effective payment below the agreed minimum commit for the applicable period, Customer shall either (a) gross-up the payment such that Redwood receives the agreed net amount, or (b) accept an adjustment to committed units/pricing for that period as set forth in the True-up schedule."

Next steps: if procurement can confirm anchor metric and PO template by end of day Tue (9/2) we’ll route the redline to Legal (Kim) and Finance (Ben) and target DocuSign by next week.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

From: Elena Park <elena@acme.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme.io
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.k@acme.com>
Date: 2025-09-01T10:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: pricing anchor, true-up cadence & EU withholding treatment

Hi Hannah —

Thanks — attaching our PO template (Acme_PO_Template.docx). A few notes from Procurement / Legal: 

- Pricing anchor: Acme prefers a device-based anchor (monthly active devices). Please translate the blended usage band to devices so Finance can model the commit.
- True-up cadence: Quarterly true-ups are acceptable.
- Net terms: Our standard practice is Net 45. Our CFO will push back on Net 60 unless we get a commercial concession elsewhere (e.g., lower first-year commit or additional onboarding credits).
- Withholding: Our EU subsidiary (Acme EU GmbH) is likely to withhold under local rules in Country X. We cannot commit to gross-up language without Legal sign-off — we would prefer Redwood to provide VAT/evidence to reclaim. If Redwood requires gross-up treatment, we will need to escalate to our tax team.

I’ve CC’d Markus (Legal) to handle the clause language. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept: (a) Net 45; and (b) a process where Acme provides withholding certificates and Redwood issues true-up credits (no gross-up).

Regards,
Elena Park
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme IoT
elena@acme.io
+44 20 7946 0123

Attachment: Acme_PO_Template.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@acme.io>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: pricing anchor, true-up cadence & EU withholding treatment

Thanks, Hannah and Elena — looping Legal in with suggested redlines below. I’m attaching a marked PDF (OrderForm_redline_kp.pdf) with inline edits. High-level positions from Redwood Legal / Commercial: 

1) Anchor metric: we can accept device-based anchor language. Update Section 2.1 to define "Anchor Units" = "monthly active devices (MAD)" and tie pricing bands to MAD thresholds. Please confirm the MAD baseline; if Acme cannot provide a baseline, we’ll use the 30-day run-rate preceding Go-Live.

2) True-up / invoicing cadence: commercial team prefers "billing in advance with quarterly true-up" for predictability. Proposed wording: "Customer will be invoiced in advance on a monthly basis. Redwood will issue a true-up invoice or credit within 30 days following the end of each calendar quarter to reconcile usage against invoiced amounts." This keeps accounting clean and reduces AR risk.

3) Net terms & one-time concession: Standard Term: Net 60. Concession: We can accept Net 45 as a one-time concession for this Order Form if Finance confirms. If Finance cannot approve, we will require a one-time onboarding credit (applied to the first invoice) to offset earlier payment timing. Either option must be documented in the Order Form Appendix A.

4) Withholding / tax evidence: Preferred Redwood position: No gross-up obligation. Proposed clause: "If Customer withholds taxes, Customer shall provide Redwood with official government withholding documentation within sixty (60) days of the payment date. Upon receipt, Redwood will (i) issue a credit for the amount withheld, or (ii) where practicable, provide supporting invoices and certifications to assist Customer with a refund claim. Customer acknowledges that routine withholding may impact the net effective payment and Redwood reserves the right to adjust committed units/pricing if material shortfalls occur and are not cured within thirty (30) days of notice."

5) PO matching and entity: Procurement must confirm which legal entity will sign and provide the PO with the exact legal entity name and tax ID. We cannot accept POs that reference a different entity than the billing entity on the Order Form.

Operational asks for Finance: Ben, can you confirm acceptance of Net 45 as a one-off concession and whether Redwood’s Finance needs the first invoice to be pre-authorized or staged? Also confirm whether we should require PO to include Redwood’s EIN for cross-border tax reclaim.

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Short answer from Finance: we can approve a one-time Net 45 concession conditional on two items: (1) Acme signs the Order Form by 2025-09-10; and (2) Acme provides a PO that references Redwood Inference LLC (EIN: XX-XXXXXXX) and indicates the billing entity. 

Operational details: first invoice should include an onboarding credit line (to offset earlier payment timing) if Legal wants to avoid changing net terms permanently. Confirm whether we want to put that credit as a dollar line on Invoice #1 or as an offset on the first quarterly true-up.
